scope: Forty fixed-practice additions, pinned point-review descendants and explicit root whole-chapter decision. Independent audits covered the new40 tasks, not a separate full-chapter certification.

changes.question: An unfamiliar Group 1 element M lies below potassium. Predict its ion charge, water products and relative reactivity. Balance M + H₂O → MOH + H₂. Can you give an exact disappearance time?
Compare lithium 2,1 with sodium 2,8,1. Explain the expected electron-loss trend and write sodium’s oxidation half-equation. Does sodium have two outer electrons because it has more shells?
At the stated room conditions, match Cl₂, Br₂ and I₂ with colour and state. Correct “iodide ions are grey-black molecules” and “iodine’s purple vapour makes its room-temperature solid purple”.

Using iodine’s supplied melting 113.7 °C and boiling 184.4 °C values at ordinary pressure, predict its stable bulk state at 150 °C. Can a higher boiling-point trend alone prove higher chemical reactivity?
Predict chlorine with iodide, bromine with chloride and iodine with bromide in the ordinary aqueous comparison. Identify the chlorine/iodide starting species and potassium’s role if KI is used.
Write the net ionic chlorine/iodide displacement equation and chlorine reduction half-equation. Can a balanced reverse iodide/chlorine equation establish its spontaneous direction?

In invented evidence, a new nonpolar-layer colour matches iodine in the same solvent after chlorine meets iodide. Another mixture simply fades after dilution. Compare the strength of these inferences and name a negative-result check.

For chlorine and iodine, explain why iodine is less reactive in this displacement comparison despite more protons. Write I₂ reduction to iodide. Why is an easier-electron-loss Group 1 answer unsuitable?
Using rounded dry-air nitrogen 78 %, oxygen 21 %, argon 0.9 %, CO₂0.04 %, calculate their volumes in an invented 500 cm³ sample. Must the four numbers sum exactly 500, or describe mass percentages?
Why does an airtight oxygen-removal model use excess moist iron and sufficient time? Is the remaining gas pure nitrogen or must all the iron react?
For a supplied teacher-controlled P₄ model, balance P₄ + O₂ → P₄O₁₀. Why should the gas be cooled before comparing volumes, and can P₂O₅ replace the product with the same coefficients?

An invented fixed flask/tube contains 80 cm³ gas, and its syringe changes 40→16 cm³ after complete oxygen removal at matched temperature/pressure. Calculate the whole-sample estimate; why is 24/40 wrong?
An oxygen-removal plan stops early, measures the final gas while warmer and compares column lengths in a tapered tube. Explain the likely issues and why close repeats do not remove them.
Balance Mg + O₂ → MgO and explain why retained oxide can have greater mass than the reacting magnesium. Does bright light alone prove a sample burned in air is pure MgO?

In an invented particle model, six H₂ molecules and four O₂ molecules react, forming only water until all hydrogen is consumed. Use 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O to count water molecules and unreacted oxygen. Check both atom totals; is carbon dioxide possible from these starting particles?
A supplied equation represents sulfur as S₈. Balance combustion to SO₂. Does consuming oxygen guarantee a comparable fall in total gas volume to the moist-iron experiment?
For supplied basic copper carbonate CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂, write its balanced thermal decomposition and explain why the pure CuCO₃ model omits a product. Is added oxygen required?
Correct “CO₂ creates heat, stops every wavelength escaping and a cold week disproves its climate effect”. Distinguish the ozone mechanism.
Two metals both show no visible cold-water reaction. Can that alone rank them? Contrast magnesium’s steam product with the hydroxide pattern of suitable cold-water metals.
Write iron with dilute HCl and name the salt oxidation state. Does copper simply evolve hydrogen more slowly? Why might an aluminium surface delay reaction?
In a suitable zinc/CuSO₄ model, identify actual reacting species, product and spectator. Is Zn²⁺ + Cu → Zn + Cu²⁺ established merely because it balances?
Balance aluminium reducing CuO under supplied suitable conditions and name the oxide reduced. Does merely mixing cold solids guarantee this reaction?
Give all eleven required metals in descending order, retaining lithium/calcium, magnesium/aluminium and silver/gold positions. Is carbon one of these metals?
An iron sample is in ordinary water with no visible air above it. Does this guarantee oxygen exclusion? Are salt and an instant brown observation necessary for rusting?
A dry-air control merely omits liquid, and a boiled-water control remains open. Explain how both controls can fail and name two conditions to keep comparable.
Scratched painted iron and intact painted iron are exposed to moisture. Explain local protection and why paint need not supply electrons or change iron’s series position.
Compare connected zinc with a separate zinc piece near wet iron. Write zinc oxidation and explain why copper is unsuitable as its sacrificial replacement.
For CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, assign oxidation/reduction and explain why heatingCuCO₃ alone is not automatically oxidation.
Write and combine zinc oxidation and copper-ion reduction. Why do electrons and sulfate not remain as new products in the net equation?
Identify both agents in zinc with Cu²⁺ and state each agent’s own change. Why is copper metal product or sulfate not the oxidizing agent?

A supplied supervised comparison changes acid concentration and exposed metal area between samples, then identifies any bubbles asH₂. Name the control repairs and gas evidence; areMg/Zn/Fe the only possible metals allowed by the source wording?
Invented collections start 0 cm³ and reach 18 cm³ in 12 s and 36 s. Calculate interval-average rates. Can equal final amounts or equal masses of different metals establish equal rate or atom amounts?
An invented ore is iron oxide mixed with iron-free rock, while another sample contains native gold grains. Which species already contains uncombined metal, and does removing rock reduce iron oxide?

Place aluminium, carbon and iron in the relevant school extraction comparison. In Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, identify the species gaining oxygen. Does every below-carbon compound need the identical iron-furnace recipe?
Explain why molten ionic bath ions and external circuit electrons have distinct roles. Write Al³⁺ reduction and correct “a carbon anode makes this simple carbon heating of alumina”.
Invented routes recover 8 kg using 48 MJ and 12 kg using 60 MJ. Compare energy per recovered kilogram and say why the lower figure alone cannot prove the best overall process.
Choose useful property links for copper wire, a copper heat exchanger and a low mass structural aluminium-alloy part. Does corrosion resistance imply no reaction in every environment?
A formable panel, hard cutting edge and moisture-exposed cutlery need different features. Name the three required steel types and correct “all stainless contains nickel and is nonmagnetic”.
An invented 5 kg iron-carbon material contains 0.60%carbon and no other elements. Calculate both masses. Does carbon being nonmetal or a change of percentage stop it qualifying as an alloy?
Using the original one-larger-atom model, explain the chain from atomic size to hardness. Must every alloy have more layers, lose metallic bonds or become impossible to deform?

independentPracticeReview: First20 source/arithmetics reviewed; near-duplicate hydrogen repaired to independently verified sixH₂/fourO₂ particle excess scenario. Remaining20 also independently checked; no substantive defect. Typography clarified. Root owns complete chapter boundary/goal/coherence decisions.
